notes: Company: mid-market SaaS that provides embedded KB widgets for B2B apps (support + help center + in-app answers).
Primary ask: hosted API for high-QPS search + rerank; keep control over cost per query; no on-prem at evaluation stage.
Indexing footprint: ~1.2M docs (help articles + community posts + transcripts) ~250M tokens after normalization; expecting incremental daily adds ~8-12k docs.
Traffic profile: steady-state high read QPS from client-side widgets: baseline 200-300 qps, peak hourly bursts up to ~1.2k qps (UTC business hours).
Latency targets: retrieval p95 <50ms, rerank + scoring budget ~50-100ms, end-to-end (retrieve+rerank+generation when used) p95 <350ms. Strict p99 guidance for SLA conversation.
Cost sensitivity: internal target total cost per query (embeddings + rerank + minimal gen) < $0.015; very focused on batching, cache hit rates, and low-cost reranker models.

Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified models for embeddings (efficient 768/1024-d vectors), reranker must be lightweight (distilled ranker) and compatible with fallback to smaller models under load.
Retrieval architecture: hybrid vector store + inverted index; want Redwood to recommend batching, prefix/KV caching, and autoscaler config to hit latency SLOs while keeping cost down.

Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs for all inference calls, optional KMS integration for keys, retention controls for user-contributed content, EU data residency for subset of customers.
Quote ask: committed QPS pricing band + overage rates and estimate for 250 qps baseline vs 1k qps; want cost model showing token/unit economics and embed store cost assumptions.
Remarks from demo: "Reranker makes big quality delta for short answers — must not add >100ms to the read path"
Sales history: initial intro 2024-09-05, product demo 2024-10-03, security questionnaire submitted 2024-10-10, technical deep-dive with SEs 2024-10-24, POC scoped 2024-11-15.
Internal sentiment: engineering excited about Redwood's runtime optimizations; procurement pushing for customer refs and clear SLA language.
Preferred decision criteria: 1) proves p95 latency under burst QPS 2) predictable cost model 3) security attestation + data residency mapping.
Ask from SE: run an ingest + retrieval stress test with our sample dataset (500k docs subset) and show embedding storage + query latency numbers.
